title_en: The Standing of the Human Being in the Sharia
body_ar: إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا من يهده الله فلا مضل ومن يضلل فلا هادي له ، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وأصحابه وسلم تسليما كثيرا (يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة وخلق منها زوجها وبث منهما رجالا كثيرا ونساء واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا) (يا أيها الذين اتقوا الله وقولوا قولا سديدا يصلح لكم أعمالكم ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم ومن يطع الله ورسوله فقد فاز فوزا عظيما)
body_en:
All praise belongs to God. We praise Him and seek His help, and we take refuge in God from the evil of our own selves and from our evil deeds. Whomever God guides, none can lead astray; whomever He leads astray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger — may God bless him, his family and his Companions, and grant them abundant peace.

{O people, be mindful of your Lord, who created you from a single soul, and created from it its mate, and spread from the two of them many men and women. Be mindful of God, in whose name you make demands of one another, and of the ties of kinship. God is ever watching over you.} (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:1)

{O you who [...] be mindful of God and speak with words that are true and sound. He will set your deeds right for you and forgive you your sins. Whoever obeys God and His Messenger has won a great triumph.} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:70–71)

flags.arabic: يا أيها الذين اتقوا الله وقولوا قولا سديدا
flags.context: The second Qur'anic verse of the sermon's opening invocation, Q 33:70.
options: Render the lacuna visibly: '{O you who [...] be mindful of God and speak with words that are true and sound}'
Restore the missing word and render '{O you who believe, be mindful of God...}' silently
Restore it but mark the restoration: '{O you who [believe], be mindful of God...}'
flags.note: The published Arabic drops آمنوا ('who believe') from Q 33:70, leaving an ungrammatical fragment (يا أيها الذين اتقوا الله). The same verse is quoted in full in articles 495 and 501, so this is a typographical loss in the source, not a variant reading. The house rule is not to fix the source silently, so the lacuna has been left visible. The Sheikh's office should confirm whether restored text may be marked in brackets.

translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.
Qur'anic renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic text of the Qur'an.
The page reproduces only the opening invocation. The two verses here are given without vowel marks, unlike the parallel openings in articles 495 and 501.
The first invocation also reads فلا مضل ('none can lead astray') without the pronoun له found in article 495; this does not change the sense.
